Around the World on Rhonda the Honda

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Meet the first woman to travel solo around the world on a motorbike

Unique Selling Point:
It's been 3 years since Steph Jeavons left her home in Wales and embarked on an impossible dream - a solo trip around the world on her motorbike, Rhonda the Honda. 41 countries and 100000km later, Steph has dealt with an attempted kidnap in Iran, ridden through civil war in Kurdistan, got caught up and nearly crushed in a Hindu pilgrimage in India, got hit by a landslide, run aground in Antarctica, hitched a ride on a Russian Ice breaker, got hit by a truck in Columbia and blown off her bike in Patagonia, to name but a few!

Summary:
Her attempt to circumnavigate the globe by crossing all seven continents is almost at an end. Africa is the final frontier, and Rhonda the Honda arrives in Durban in early August. From there, she and Steph will ride down the coast to Cape Town where they will meet up with another famous British motorcyclist, Charlie Boorman.

Further information:
Steph plans to leave Cape Town by the end of August and head straight up the cost to Namibia. She has filmed extensively on her journey, and also writes a popular blog that is read by thousands every day. onestephbeyond.com

Extra Budget Items:
Trip to Cape Town - airfares, accommodation, car hire

Press Release:


Around the world on Rhonda
It's been 3 years since Steph Jeavons left her home in Wales and embarked on an impossible dream - a
solo trip around the world on her motorbike, Rhonda the Honda. Crossing through 41 countries and
covering over 100 000km, Steph finally rode into Cape Town on Rhonda. And meeting her at the end of the
line – the Carte Blanche crew and legendary British motorcyclist Charley Boorman.

Script:


RHONDA THE HONDA

V/O: Meet Steph Jeavons, a fearless adventurer from Wales who is riding around the world on a 250cc motorbike called Rhonda the Honda.

Steph: Anyone who has ever got on a motorbike has had that desire really to just get on it and ride into the sunset.

Link: It’s one thing to feel the urge to embark on a life of adventure, but quite another to act on it – even more so when it involves biking solo across seven continents for more than three-and-a-half years.

Steph: My original dream was to ride to Borneo to see the Orangutans – that was it. I just wanted to go and see the wildlife. Then I thought if I ride to Borneo I might as well carry on to Australia; if I ride to Australia, I might as well carry on, and that was it. A couple of tequilas later and I was going to ride the 7 continents, you know!

V/O: She left London’s iconic Ace Café in March 2014, and rode across Europe, through Turkey and into Iran, a country most of us would regard as dangerous.

Steph: Everybody is scared of their neighbours, everybody’s saying we’re ok, but watch out for those guys, they will kill you. And so the Turks were warning as you’re going through the mountains – don’t stop for anything. So eventually of course, I ran out of fuel. and these scary Kurds turn up and take me home, feed me and teach me about the Kurdish traditions and I teach them about the Welsh traditions. It was a great experience, and the next morning they took me and the bike to the nearest garage, they washed the bike. That’s the one thing I’ve learned about men all over the world: they see a woman with a motorbike, they clean the motorbike, they want to know if you’re married? They want to know how much the bike is worth, how fast it goes? And they want to fix it even if it’s not broken. So I’ve had to literally push people away trying to fix things that aren’t broken. “We must change the fork seals!” And I’m like no, really they’re fine, you know.

V/O: After 42 countries, Iran now rates as one of Steph’s favourites, and it is India she regards as one of the most challenging.

Steph: It’s like riding on a knife-edge, it’s about survival, but it’s amazing! It’s like playing Grand Theft Auto in real life, you know. It’s like you’re in the game, and I love that.

V/O Her route took her over the Himalayas, on some of the most scenic mountain roads in the world, through Asia and down to Borneo where she finally met the Orangutangs.

Steph;

From there she crossed into Australia, amusing herself through the never-ending Outback by dancing in the saddle.

V/O: After flying to Argentina, she rode 4000km to the tip of South America in pursuit of her ultimate goal: Antarctica. That meant having to cross the Drake Passage, one of the roughest seas in the world.

Steph: The only people that would agree to take me was on a 60-foot sailing yacht and I had to become part of the crew. So, I was terrified, I must say. I thought if I can just get on the boat and we leave, then there is nothing I can do about it, I’ve just got to go with it. So, it took 5 days, I was horribly sick for the first two days, I couldn’t move. I had a little jar that I unscrewed and threw up in, it was horrific. And then once we got closer to Antarctica we’d have to take it in turns to watch out for icebergs. But then it was a lot calmer once we arrived, and it was so worth it. It was stunning to see Antarctica.

V/O: After dropping anchor, the Crew loaded Rhonda into a rubber dinghy and headed for Paradise harbour.

Steph: “So far, so good. It was all going smoothly and I was growing in confidence that we might just be able to pull this off. But one wrong move now in this ice-cold water and things could get serious very quickly. With good teamwork and the usual brute force and ignorance we actually made it.”

V/O: Steph and Rhonda the Honda had finally reached the remotest continent.

Steph: “And boy, did it feel good. Whoo hoo!”

Steph: And actually, a woman on a motorbike in Antarctica carries a lot of weight, you know. We radioed ahead, and they were like “You have a woman? And a motorbike?” I’m not sure which one was more exciting, I think probably the motorbike. So, there was a lot of help, and then once we had landed her once we continued around the peninsula and there was a Ukrainian science base.

John: Tell us more about the Ukrainian scientists?

Steph: They count penguins, they look at the weather, and they drink a lot. They do drink a lot; they have lots of vodka and 5000-year-old ice cubes, you know. They helped us get the bike ashore; we all had a play in the snow and then they we got her into the base so they could get a picture of her into the base. They put on a big spread of food and beer, and we sang songs and played drinking games, it was absolutely brilliant! It was not what I expected of Antarctica.

John: It sounds like you like a party too?

Steph: I’m Welsh, we are very similar in that sense.

V/O: To get back to South America they hitched a ride on a Russian icebreaker. After riding up the Pacific coast of both South and North America, Steph decided to rest up in Canada for a few months.

Steph: It’s a solo ride, I’m riding alone but you’re never really alone. Being a biker you are part of a network – a worldwide network – and I’ve been picked up along the way so many times. I’ve stayed with every different type of religion, I’ve stayed with rich with poor, I’ve slept on floors and in posh houses, and everybody welcomed me. It’s really humbling.

V/O: After riding across Canada, they had covered 100 000km with no mechanical problems. Rhonda was crated and put on a ship bound for South Africa and the seventh continent. And in Cape Town they met up with an old friend, celebrity biker, Charley Boorman.

Link: Adventure biking has attracted a global following and much of that is thanks to Charley Boorman, who together with world famous movie star Ewan McGregor, has blazed a trail for people wanting to satisfy their wanderlust.

V/O: The TV series “Long Way Round” documented their incredible journey circumnavigating the globe, and “Long Way Down” continued the adventure through Africa. Charley was in Cape Town to lead a bike tour to Victoria Falls.

Charley: When you say to people, I’m going off to SA to go riding, they go, ooh that’s a dodgy place and you go is it? and they go yes, terribly dangerous and then have you been there? No.

John: Are you like a bear with a sore tooth when you’re not riding or adventuring?

Charley: If I spend too much time at home I start to get itchy feet and I think my wife does as well. The other day I found my suitcase down by the front door. I think she was hinting that I’ve been here long enough now Charley.

John: How many bikes do you have?

Charley: My wife is going to watch this so I can’t tell you, more than one.
I think I have a dozen or so bikes.

V/O: Even though Charley has travelled the world on two wheels, he had a BBC budget and the support of a television crew. But Steph’s journey has been completely solo, without support.

John: Knowing what you know, do you think Steph is a bit mad or do you understand?

Charley: No I think she’s crazy, I’m a little jealous because she’s been to quite a few more places than I have. She’s a fascinating person. I think it’s probably harder for a woman to travel by themselves.

Steph: A lot of people think it’s harder as a woman. I’ve never done it as a guy so I can’t compare. But once you get out there, people are not seeing a victim on a bike, they’re seeing a strong woman. And even in countries where people have told me to pretend to be married and to say that my husband is on his way, I’ve refused to do that and just said no, I’m married to my motorbike, and the response is amazing. People say yes, high five, you go girl.

V/O: And Steph is off on the last leg of her epic journey – up Africa, and all the way home – with Rhonda the Honda and the open road.

PROMOS

Promo 1 – 15”

V/O: She’s been on the road for almost 4 years; she’s travelled over a hundred thousand kilometres, through 42 countries, on seven continents, and she’s still going strong.

Meet Steph Jeavons and a plucky little motorbike called Rhonda the Honda


Promo 2 – 15”

V/O: He’s taken the Long Way Round, and the Long Way Down. Now celebrity biker Charley Boorman meets up with Steph Jeavons on her epic round the world journey.

Charley: I think if you thought about the risk of what could happen, you’d never end up doing anything.


Promo 3 – 10”

V/O: Ever wanted to drop everything and hit the road? We’re in Cape Town with Steph Jeavons and Charley Boorman – adventure bikers with thousands of miles behind them.
